:::{#def-data-splits}
#### Training/validation/test split

A **training/validation/test split** divides the data into three sets:

- Use the *training set* to estimate model parameters.
- Use the *validation set* to compare candidate models,
  choose transformations,
  or tune hyperparameters.
- Use the *test set* once at the end
  to estimate final out-of-sample performance.

::: {.attribution}
Source: adapted from the rme notes' section [Train/validation/test splits](https://morrison-lab.github.io/rme/chapters/Linear-models-overview.html#trainvalidationtest-splits),
which follows @james2021islr2e [pp. 198--201].
:::

:::

::: notes
This validation approach extends the basic train/test split
by separating model tuning
from final model assessment.
It follows @james2021islr2e [pp. 198-201].

Keeping the test set untouched during model building
helps avoid optimistic bias
from repeatedly trying many models.
In @exr-data-splits,
a rule of 60% / 20% / 20% on $n = 32$ cars
gives sets of 19, 6, and 7 cars,
and the 7 test cars are used only once, after the model is chosen.
:::
